title: Carbonyl groups in X and Y: double decarboxylation of a beta-keto diacid and the cyclic anhydride of a cis-1,2-diacid
summary: Two diacids are heated, and every reaction is watched at two levels at once: the flask on the left, the molecules on the right, in step. Flask 1 (2,4-dimethyl-3-oxopentanedioic acid) fizzes CO2 into limewater while curved arrows run each six-membered cyclic decarboxylation and the acid-catalysed keto-enol tautomerism, twice, to pentan-3-one. Flask 2 (cis-4-oxocyclopentane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid) gives off water that turns anhydrous copper sulfate blue while the hydroxyl attacks, a tetrahedral intermediate forms, a proton moves and water leaves to close the cyclic anhydride. Products come from pushing the arrows on the molecule graphs; the C=O groups are then counted. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Carboxylic acids on heating - decarboxylation of beta-keto acids and cyclic anhydrides from cis-1,2-diacids
subtopics: Beta-keto acid decarboxylation through a six-membered cyclic transition state
Counting carbonyl groups in ketones, acids and anhydrides
concepts: Reactant 1 is a double beta-keto acid: each CO2H is on a carbon alpha to the ketone
Heat: three curved arrows around a six-membered ring give CO2 and an enol, which tautomerises to the ketone; this happens twice, giving pentan-3-one (1 C=O)
Reactant 2 has its CO2H groups on C3 and C4 - not a beta-keto acid, so no CO2 is lost
The two CO2H are cis (wedged ring bonds): one OH attacks the other C=O, a proton transfers and water leaves, closing a five-membered cyclic anhydride (1 ketone + 2 anhydride C=O = 3)
Sum = 1 + 3 = 4; the water comes from an OH oxygen, so no C=O is lost in forming Y

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: X = pentan-3-one (1 C=O), Y = cyclic anhydride (3 C=O), sum 4
The drawing decoded: the wedged ring bonds rebuilt as a mol block, read by RDKit and embedded in 3-D - both CO2H on the same face (cis, meso)

RDKit reaction templates: beta-keto acid decarboxylation repeated until none is left gives pentan-3-one after 2 CO2; 1,2-diacid dehydration gives the cis-fused anhydride; neither template fires on the wrong reactant
SMARTS count: 1 C=O in X, 3 in Y; atoms balance for both reactions
MMFF: the trans-fused anhydride is about 17 kcal/mol above the cis-fused one
Custom controls: no methyls gives acetone; a gamma-keto acid loses no CO2 (6); trans diacid makes no anhydride but still 4; no heat gives 6
Independent script tests/verify_p1q11.py: 25 of 25 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q43) gives 4
